title: Errands
goal: Get everyday jobs done around town on your own: take out cash, sort out a SIM card, get your phone fixed, clothes stitched and washed, your hair cut and a parcel sent.
intro:
Living somewhere means errands: the ATM that's out of cash, the SIM card that stops working, the cracked screen, the kurta at the tailor's, the clothes at the ironing stall, the parcel for your mum. In India most of these jobs are done for you by someone at a small local shop, and the key verb for that is the **causative**: not करना 'do' but **करवाना** 'get it done'.

In this unit you'll learn to say what you need to get done, who you get to do it, and to ask the question every Indian errand ends with: **कब तक हो जाएगा?** 'When will it be ready?'

grammar.title: Getting something done: the causative -वाना
grammar.body:
English says *I got my hair cut* or *I had my phone fixed*. Hindi does this with one verb: add **-वाना** to the root of a verb and it means 'have someone else do it'.

करना 'do' → **करवाना** 'get done'
बनाना 'make' → **बनवाना** 'get made'
भेजना 'send' → **भिजवाना** 'get sent'
काटना 'cut' → **कटवाना** 'get cut'
धोना 'wash' → **धुलवाना** 'get washed'
सीना 'stitch' → **सिलवाना** 'get stitched'
खोलना 'open' → **खुलवाना** 'get opened'
बदलना 'change' → **बदलवाना** 'get changed'

Notice that a long vowel in the root usually gets **shorter**: ā → a (काट → कट), e → i (भेज → भिज), o → u (धो → धुल, खोल → खुल).

**Who does the work** takes **से**: मैंने **दर्ज़ी से** कुर्ता सिलवाया 'I had the tailor stitch a kurta'. Often you just leave the person out.

The causative is an ordinary transitive verb: it takes **ने** in the past and agrees with the object (मैंने स्क्रीन **बदलवाई** — स्क्रीन is f). It's also how you use English verbs: **रिपेयर करवाना, रिचार्ज करवाना, चेक करवाना**. **करवाना** and **कराना** mean the same; both are common.

**The trap:** मैंने बाल **काटे** means *I* cut the hair (yours? my own?). At the barber's it's **कटवाए**. In the same way, you **open** a bank account with खुलवाना, because the bank does it.

grammar.title: Verb families: बनना → बनाना → बनवाना
grammar.body:
Many Hindi verbs come in sets of three that share a root:

**1. it happens** (no doer, intransitive): **बनना** 'get made, get ready'
**2. someone does it** (transitive): **बनाना** 'make'
**3. someone gets it done** (causative): **बनवाना** 'get it made'

कुर्ता **बन** गया — the kurta is ready.
दर्ज़ी ने कुर्ता **बनाया** — the tailor made the kurta.
मैंने कुर्ता **बनवाया** — I had the kurta made.

More families you'll need for errands:
कटना / काटना / कटवाना — cut
धुलना / धोना / धुलवाना — wash
खुलना / खोलना / खुलवाना — open
सिलना / सीना / सिलवाना — stitch
ठीक होना / ठीक करना / ठीक करवाना — get fixed / fix / get fixed by someone

When you ask about the **thing** — is it ready, is it fixed, is it washed — use the first verb, usually with जाना: **कब तक बन जाएगा?** 'when will it be ready?', **फ़ोन ठीक हो गया?** 'is the phone fixed?', **कपड़े धुल गए?** 'are the clothes washed?'.

**The trap:** the first verb never takes **ने**, because nobody is doing anything in that sentence: say कुर्ता बन गया, never कुर्ते ने बना. And don't use बनाया when you mean 'it's ready': अभी नहीं **बना** 'it isn't ready yet'.

grammar.title: मुझे … है: the infinitive agrees with the thing
grammar.body:
You know **मुझे + infinitive + है** for 'I have to / I need to' (unit 15): **मुझे जाना है** 'I need to go'. Errands are full of it.

When the infinitive has an **object**, in careful Hindi the infinitive changes to agree with that object, like an adjective:

masculine singular → **-ना**: मुझे फ़ॉर्म **भरना** है
feminine → **-नी**: मुझे सिम **लेनी** है, मुझे दाढ़ी **बनवानी** है
masculine plural → **-ने**: मुझे पैसे **निकालने** हैं, मुझे बाल **कटवाने** हैं

The **है/हैं** agrees too: पैसे and बाल are plural, so **हैं**.

In fast everyday speech many people just say मुझे सिम लेना है — you'll hear both, and nobody will mind. But the agreeing form is the standard one and sounds educated, so aim for it.

The same goes for चाहिए with an infinitive and for 'want to' with लेना/करना: **आपको कितने पैसे जमा करने हैं?** 'How much money do you want to pay in?'

culture: Most errands in an Indian city happen at small neighbourhood shops where the same people know you for years — the phone shop that does recharges, SIMs and repairs, the **मास्टर जी** tailor, the **धोबी** or **इस्त्री वाला** ironing clothes with a heavy iron at a table on the pavement, the local **नाई** whose haircut often ends with a free head massage (**चंपी**). Shopkeepers your age or older are **भैया** (or **दीदी**, **आंटी**), and you can switch to **तुम** with the ones you see every week; in a bank or a smart salon stay with **आप**. Services are rarely bargained over, but always ask **कब तक हो जाएगा?** and expect 'कल पक्का' ('tomorrow, for sure') to mean 'probably the day after'. Getting a SIM needs ID (Aadhaar for Indians, a passport and visa for foreigners). Almost everywhere you can pay by UPI — just ask **स्कैन कर दूँ?** 'shall I scan?' — and ATMs running out of cash before festivals is a classic.

lessons.title: At the bank and the ATM

tip.title: मुझे पैसे निकालने हैं — I need to…
tip.body:
- **मुझे + infinitive + है** = 'I need to': मुझे बैंक **जाना** है.
- With an object, the infinitive agrees with the **thing**: फ़ॉर्म **भरना** है (m) · सिम **लेनी** है (f) · पैसे **निकालने** हैं (pl).
- Plural thing → **हैं**. In fast speech people often keep -ना, but the agreeing form is standard.

lessons.title: Phone trouble: SIMs and repairs

tip.title: करवाना — getting it done
tip.body:
- Add **-वाना** to a verb root: 'have someone do it'. करना → **करवाना**, बदलना → **बदलवाना**, भेजना → **भिजवाना**.
- Who does the work takes **से**: मैं इन भैया **से** फ़ोन ठीक करवाता हूँ.
- English verbs too: **रिपेयर करवाना, रिचार्ज करवाना**.
- Past: **ने** + agreement with the thing: मैंने स्क्रीन **बदलवाई** (f).

sentences.roman: fon bahut purānā hai, skrīn bhī ṭūṭ gaī hai.
sentences.en: The phone's really old, and the screen is cracked too.

lessons.title: At the tailor's: is it ready yet?

tip.title: बनना · बनाना · बनवाना
tip.body:
- Verbs come in families: **बनना** 'get made' (no doer) → **बनाना** 'make' → **बनवाना** 'get it made'.
- Ask about the *thing* with the first one: कब तक **बन** जाएगा? फ़ोन **ठीक हो** गया?
- Same pattern: कटना/काटना/कटवाना, धुलना/धोना/धुलवाना, खुलना/खोलना/खुलवाना.
- The first verb never takes **ने**: कुर्ता बन गया.
tip.pattern: thing + बन / हो / धुल + जाएगा / गया

sentences.native: भैया, मेरा कुर्ता बन गया?
sentences.roman: bhaiyā, merā kurtā ban gayā?
sentences.en: Is my kurta ready?

sentences.native: मुझे दर्ज़ी से एक कुर्ता बनवाना है।
sentences.roman: mujhe darzī se ek kurtā banvānā hai.
sentences.en: I want to get a kurta made at the tailor's.

sentences.native: दर्ज़ी ने मेरा नाप लिया।
sentences.roman: darzī ne merā nāp liyā.
sentences.en: The tailor took my measurements.

sentences.native: मैंने दो कमीज़ें सिलवाईं।
sentences.roman: maiṃne do kamīzeṃ silvāīṃ.
sentences.en: I had two shirts made.

sentences.native: कमीज़ें कब तक सिल जाएँगी?
sentences.roman: kamīzeṃ kab tak sil jāyeṃgī?
sentences.en: When will the shirts be ready?

sentences.native: मुझे यह पैंट छोटी करवानी है।
sentences.roman: mujhe yah paiṇṭ chhoṭī karvānī hai.
sentences.en: I need to get these trousers shortened.

sentences.native: नहीं, अभी नहीं बना, कल आइए।
sentences.roman: nahīṃ, abhī nahīṃ banā, kal āiye.
sentences.en: No, it's not ready yet, come tomorrow.

sentences.native: मुझे यह कल तक चाहिए, शादी है।
sentences.roman: mujhe yah kal tak chāhiye, shādī hai.
sentences.en: I need it by tomorrow, there's a wedding.

sentences.native: आपका फ़ोन ठीक हो गया, ले जाइए।
sentences.roman: āpkā fon ṭhīk ho gayā, le jāiye.
sentences.en: Your phone's fixed, you can take it.

sentences.native: दर्ज़ी ने कुर्ता बहुत अच्छा बनाया है।
sentences.roman: darzī ne kurtā bahut achchhā banāyā hai.
sentences.en: The tailor has done a great job on the kurta.

sentences.native: दुकान दस बजे खुलेगी।
sentences.roman: dukān das baje khulegī.
sentences.en: The shop will open at ten.

sentences.native: ठीक है, कल शाम तक मिल जाएगा ना?
sentences.roman: ṭhīk hai, kal shām tak mil jāyegā nā?
sentences.en: OK, I'll have it by tomorrow evening, right?

lessons.title: At the barber's or the salon

tip.title: Telling the barber what you want
tip.body:
- Say what you want done with **-वाना**: मुझे बाल **कटवाने** हैं, दाढ़ी **बनवानी** है (a shave = 'get the beard made').
- Then steer with **कर दीजिए / कर दो**: पीछे से थोड़े छोटे **कर दीजिए**.
- 'Don't' is **मत**: ज़्यादा छोटे **मत** करना.
- With your regular barber, **भैया** + तुम is normal; in a smart salon, आप.

sentences.native: मैं हर महीने बाल कटवाता हूँ।
sentences.roman: maiṃ har mahīne bāl kaṭvātā hūṃ.
sentences.en: I get my hair cut every month. (man)

sentences.native: भैया, ज़्यादा छोटे मत करना।
sentences.roman: bhaiyā, zyādā chhoṭe mat karnā.
sentences.en: Don't cut it too short, OK?

sentences.native: मुझे दाढ़ी भी बनवानी है।
sentences.roman: mujhe dāṛhī bhī banvānī hai.
sentences.en: I want a shave as well.

sentences.native: पास में कोई अच्छा नाई है?
sentences.roman: pās meṃ koī achchhā nāī hai?
sentences.en: Is there a good barber's near here?

sentences.native: मेरी बहन पार्लर गई है, बाल कटवाने।
sentences.roman: merī bahan pārlar gaī hai, bāl kaṭvāne.
sentences.en: My sister's gone to the salon to get her hair cut.

sentences.native: तुमने बाल कहाँ से कटवाए? बहुत अच्छे लग रहे हैं!
sentences.roman: tumne bāl kahāṃ se kaṭvāye? bahut achchhe lag rahe haiṃ!
sentences.en: Where did you get your hair cut? It looks great!

sentences.native: पीछे से थोड़े छोटे कर दीजिए, ऊपर से नहीं।
sentences.roman: pīchhe se thoṛe chhoṭe kar dījiye, ūpar se nahīṃ.
sentences.en: Take a bit off the back, not the top.

sentences.native: नाई ने बहुत छोटे कर दिए!
sentences.roman: nāī ne bahut chhoṭe kar diye!
sentences.en: The barber cut it way too short!

sentences.native: पार्लर में कितना लगता है?
sentences.roman: pārlar meṃ kitnā lagtā hai?
sentences.en: How much does it cost at the salon?

lessons.title: Laundry and the chemist

tip.title: कर देना — a friendly request for later
tip.body:
- The plain infinitive is a soft request, often for later: इस्त्री **कर देना** 'iron these, will you?', कल **आ जाना** 'come tomorrow, OK?'
- It's friendly (तुम level). For आप, add **-इएगा**: भर **दीजिएगा**.
- 'Don't forget' = **मत भूलना**.

new: यह दवा बिना पर्ची के मिलेगी?

sentences.native: भैया, कल तक कपड़े दे देना।
sentences.roman: bhaiyā, kal tak kapṛe de denā.
sentences.en: Have the clothes back to me by tomorrow, OK?

sentences.native: मैं अपने कपड़े धोबी से धुलवाती हूँ।
sentences.roman: maiṃ apne kapṛe dhobī se dhulvātī hūṃ.
sentences.en: I get my clothes washed by the dhobi. (woman)

sentences.native: यह कुर्ता इस्त्री कर देना, कल पहनना है।
sentences.roman: yah kurtā istrī kar denā, kal pahannā hai.
sentences.en: Iron this kurta, will you? I'm wearing it tomorrow.

sentences.native: इस्त्री वाले को ये कपड़े दे आना।
sentences.roman: istrī vāle ko ye kapṛe de ānā.
sentences.en: Drop these clothes off with the ironing man.

sentences.native: केमिस्ट से मेरी दवा ले आना।
sentences.roman: kemisṭ se merī davā le ānā.
sentences.en: Pick up my medicine from the chemist, will you?

sentences.native: पर्ची लाना मत भूलना।
sentences.roman: parchī lānā mat bhūlnā.
sentences.en: Don't forget to bring the prescription.

sentences.native: धोबी को पैसे दे देना, मैं घर पर नहीं हूँ।
sentences.roman: dhobī ko paise de denā, maiṃ ghar par nahīṃ hūṃ.
sentences.en: Pay the dhobi, will you? I'm not home.

sentences.native: कल सुबह आठ बजे आ जाना।
sentences.roman: kal subah āṭh baje ā jānā.
sentences.en: Come at eight tomorrow morning, OK?

sentences.native: आप यह फ़ॉर्म भर दीजिएगा।
sentences.roman: āp yah form bhar dījiyegā.
sentences.en: Would you fill in this form, please?

sentences.native: सॉरी, यह दवा बिना पर्ची के नहीं मिलती।
sentences.roman: sorī, yah davā binā parchī ke nahīṃ miltī.
sentences.en: Sorry, this medicine isn't sold without a prescription.

sentences.native: पास में कोई केमिस्ट खुला है?
sentences.roman: pās meṃ koī kemisṭ khulā hai?
sentences.en: Is there a chemist open nearby?

sentences.native: मेरे कपड़े धुल गए?
sentences.roman: mere kapṛe dhul gaye?
sentences.en: Have my clothes been washed?

lessons.title: Sending a parcel
new: यह पार्सल दिल्ली भेजना है, कितना लगेगा?

sentences.native: मुझे यह पार्सल माँ को भिजवाना है।
sentences.roman: mujhe yah pārsal māṃ ko bhijvānā hai.
sentences.en: I need to get this parcel sent to Mum.

sentences.native: कूरियर वाला कब आएगा?
sentences.roman: kūriyar vālā kab āyegā?
sentences.en: When is the courier coming?

sentences.native: पार्सल कब तक पहुँच जाएगा?
sentences.roman: pārsal kab tak pahuṃch jāyegā?
sentences.en: When will the parcel get there?

sentences.native: वे कल तक पहुँचा देंगे।
sentences.roman: ve kal tak pahuṃchā deṃge.
sentences.en: They'll deliver it by tomorrow.

sentences.native: मैंने माँ के लिए मिठाई भिजवाई।
sentences.roman: maiṃne māṃ ke liye miṭhāī bhijvāī.
sentences.en: I had some sweets sent to Mum.

sentences.native: अंदर क्या है? — कपड़े और किताबें।
sentences.roman: andar kyā hai? — kapṛe aur kitābeṃ.
sentences.en: What's inside? — Clothes and books.

sentences.native: पार्सल पर पता साफ़ लिखिए।
sentences.roman: pārsal par patā sāf likhiye.
sentences.en: Write the address clearly on the parcel.

sentences.native: तुम्हारा पार्सल आ गया, मैंने ले लिया।
sentences.roman: tumhārā pārsal ā gayā, maiṃne le liyā.
sentences.en: Your parcel came, I took it in.

sentences.native: कूरियर से भेजो, जल्दी पहुँचेगा।
sentences.roman: kūriyar se bhejo, jaldī pahuṃchegā.
sentences.en: Send it by courier, it'll get there faster.
